title: 見つけやすい落とし物箱

paragraphs.english: A school kept lost objects in a deep box beside the teachers' room. Students were allowed to look inside during lunch. [A] However, small things often disappeared under jackets and sports bags, so finding an object took a long time. One month, the student council sorted the contents. They found eleven water bottles, nine pencil cases, and many single gloves. [B] The council decided that a single box was no longer useful. They borrowed three low shelves and put a label on each one. Bottles went on the top shelf, pencil cases on the middle shelf, and clothes below. [C] A photograph of the shelves was added to the school website every Friday. Students could check it at home before coming to search. Objects that stayed for a month received a date tag so the school could contact classes again before moving them into storage. [D] Within two weeks, more than half of the old objects had been claimed by their owners.
paragraphs.translation: 学校の深い落とし物箱は昼休みに見られるが、上から見えるのは大きい物が中心だった。小物は服やかばんの下に隠れ探しにくい。生徒会が分けると水筒十一、筆箱九、片手の手袋などがあった。一箱では不便なので低い棚三段を借り表示し、上に水筒、中に筆箱、下に衣服を置いた。金曜には棚の写真を学校サイトに載せ自宅で確認できた。一か月残る物は日付札を付け、保管庫へ移す前に再度クラスへ連絡した。二週間で古い物の半数以上が持ち主に戻った。

paragraphs.english: The running club practiced in a park with several crossing paths. New members sometimes took a wrong turn and returned later than expected. [A] The captain, Ella, knew the route so well that she had not noticed how confusing it could be. She walked it slowly with two new runners and asked them where they felt unsure. Both stopped at a path beside a large stone. [B] Ella took a photograph of that crossing and drew an arrow showing the correct direction. She made similar picture cards for two other places. Before the next practice, everyone looked at the cards together. [C] The club did not paint permanent arrows on the park paths because other groups used different routes. Instead, new members carried a small copy of the picture guide. After a few weeks, they no longer needed it. [D] Ella saved the cards for future members and added a reminder to check the guide whenever the park changed a path or sign.
paragraphs.translation: 公園の交差路で陸上部の新人は道を間違えることがあった。慣れた主将エラは混乱に気づかず、新人二人とゆっくり歩き迷う箇所を尋ねた。大石の交差点で二人とも止まり、二方向が同じほどよく使われた道に見えた。彼女は写真に正しい矢印を描き、他二か所もカードにした。次回全員で見て、新人が小さな案内を携帯した。他団体は別経路なので恒久的に道へ矢印を塗らなかった。数週で不要になっても将来の新人用に保存し、公園の道や看板変更時に確認する注意も足した。

paragraphs.english: Before a class trip, students were asked to prepare short guides to places they would visit. Most groups made written sheets with maps and facts. [A] One group wanted to record an audio guide because some classmates liked listening while looking at buildings. They wrote a script about an old gate near the station. Their first recording lasted eight minutes and included every fact they had found. [B] During a test, listeners could not tell when they should look up, turn left, or move closer. The group realized that a guide needed to connect information with what people could actually see. They shortened the history section and added pauses after directions. [C] They also started each part by naming one visible feature, such as the clock above the entrance. The next test was easier to follow. [D] On the trip, students could choose the audio or written guide. The group kept both because listening was helpful for some situations but reading a map was better for others.
paragraphs.translation: 旅行先の短い案内を用意する課題で、多くは地図と事実の紙を作った。一組は建物を見ながら聴きたい人向けに駅そばの古い門の音声案内を作った。初回は調べた全事実を詰め込み八分だったが、聴き手が周囲を見る時間がほぼなかった。試すと見上げる、曲がる、近づく時が不明だった。そこで実際に見える物と説明を結び、歴史部分を短くして方向指示に間を入れ、入口上の時計など見える特徴から始めた。次は分かりやすくなった。本番は音声か紙を選べ、状況により地図が便利なので両方残した。

paragraphs.english: The art room had a sunny window where students displayed paper models. Visitors could see them from the corridor, and the colors looked bright in the afternoon. [A] After several weeks, however, one student noticed that the side facing the window had become much paler. She turned the model around and compared it with the side that had faced the room. The difference was easy to see. [B] The class did not want to hide all its work in a cupboard. They discussed ways to keep the display visible without leaving the same objects in strong sunlight every day. They decided to change the models each week and move the display away from the glass. [C] Photographs of earlier work stayed on a board in the corridor, so visitors could still see the full project. The teacher asked students to record which materials changed most. [D] Their art display had also become a small observation project about the effect of light on different kinds of paper.

paragraphs.english: A school cafe opened for one afternoon during the festival. Students took orders at the counter and carried drinks to tables. At first, every order was written on a small white slip. [A] The kitchen team sometimes prepared the same drink twice because it could not tell which slips had already been completed. The leader tried putting finished slips in a separate box, but the counter quickly became crowded. A student suggested making a clear mark on each slip before a drink left the kitchen. [B] The team chose a large circle in blue ink because it was easy to see even from a short distance. They practiced the new method before the busiest hour began. [C] One person read an order, another made the drink, and a third checked the table number and marked the slip. The number of repeated orders fell. [D] At the final meeting, the team said that a shared, visible signal had worked better than asking everyone to remember which jobs were done.

paragraphs.english: In an English class, students read a story about two friends who missed the last bus. The printed story ended when they began walking home. Their teacher asked each group to write what happened next. [A] One group wrote a funny ending in which the friends met a traveling singer. Another imagined that they found a bicycle and took turns riding it. A third group wrote a quiet conversation about an argument earlier that day. [B] When the groups read their endings aloud, students noticed that each one used a different detail from the original story. The singer idea came from a poster mentioned near the beginning. The bicycle came from a shop in the background, and the argument came from a short line of dialogue. [C] The teacher asked the class to explain these connections instead of voting for only one best ending. [D] Students learned that creative writing could begin with careful reading, and that the same text could support several different ideas when writers could show their reasons.
paragraphs.translation: 英語の授業で終バスを逃した友人二人の物語を読み、歩き始めて終わる続きを各班が書いた。旅の歌手と会う楽しい結末、自転車を交代する結末、昼間の口論を静かに話す結末が生まれた。声に出すと各班が元の違う細部を使ったと分かった。歌手は冒頭のポスター、自転車は背景の店、口論は短いせりふが手がかりだった。どれも無関係な想像だけではない。先生は一位を投票する代わりに結びつきを説明させた。創作も精読から始まり、理由を示せれば同じ本文から複数の案が生まれると学んだ。

paragraphs.english: A nature center gave visitors a map with three walking routes. The shortest route was drawn in green, the middle one in orange, and the longest in red. [A] One visitor explained that she could not easily tell the green line from the red one. She had followed the wrong route and walked farther than she intended. The staff thanked her for telling them and looked at the map again. [B] They added a different pattern to each line: dots, short marks, and a solid line. They also wrote the route names beside the lines at several points. [C] Before printing many copies, they asked visitors to try the revised map and describe how they chose a path. The patterns helped even when a copy was printed without color. [D] The staff kept the colors as well, because many visitors found them useful. The new map gave people more than one way to understand the same information instead of depending on a single visual feature.
paragraphs.translation: 自然センターは短・中・長の道を緑・橙・赤で示す地図を配った。ある利用者は緑と赤を見分けにくく、意図より長く歩いたと伝えた。職員は礼を言い見直し、色だけに頼らない方法が必要と考えた。点線、短い線の列、実線を追加し各所に経路名も書いた。大量印刷前に利用者へ試してもらうと白黒でも有効だった。色も役立つ人が多いので残し、一つの視覚的特徴だけに依存せず複数の理解手段を提供した。

title: お祝いの食卓を準備する

paragraphs.english: For her grandfather's birthday, Anna wanted to cook the same meal her family had enjoyed the previous year. She found a recipe in her notebook and began making a shopping list. [A] Her brother reminded her that two cousins would also come this time. One was bringing a small child, and the other would arrive after work. Anna looked at the old plan and realized that repeating it exactly might not suit the new group. [B] She chose a main dish that could stay warm and put a few simple foods on separate plates. That way, people could choose what they wanted and late arrivals could still eat comfortably. [C] She also asked each guest to bring a photograph to share with her grandfather. During dinner, the stories around the photographs became the busiest part of the evening. [D] Anna was glad she had kept the feeling of the old celebration without trying to copy every detail. The family made a new memory rather than repeating an old schedule.
paragraphs.translation: 祖父の誕生日にアンナは前年と同じ料理を作ろうとレシピを見つけ買い物リストを始めた。兄に今回はいとこ二人と幼児も来て、一人は仕事後だと言われ、同じ計画は合わないと気づいた。献立と時間を調整し、保温できる主菜と別皿の簡単な食べ物で各自が選べ、遅着でも食べやすくした。客には祖父と見る写真も頼み、夕食は写真の思い出話で最もにぎわった。細部をまねず昔の温かさを残せて喜び、古い予定を再現するのでなく新しい思い出を作った。

paragraphs.english: After a class visited a farm, their teacher asked them to write questions they still had. Most reports from earlier trips had simply listed what students had seen. [A] This time, a girl asked why the farmer planted different vegetables in the same field at different times of year. A boy wanted to know how the farmer decided when to sell his crops. Other students asked about the tools stored in a shed they had passed. [B] The teacher collected the questions and sent a short list to the farmer. He replied with a letter and three photographs showing work during another season. [C] The class compared these with the photographs from their own visit. They realized that one afternoon had shown only a small part of a year's work. [D] In their final reports, students explained both what they had observed and what they had learned later. The teacher planned to use the same question stage after future trips so that returning to school would not mean the end of learning about a place.
paragraphs.translation: 農場見学後、先生はまだ残る疑問を書かせた。以前の報告は見た物の列挙が多かったが、今回は季節で野菜を変える理由、販売時期の決め方、納屋の道具などを質問した。先生が一覧を農家に送ると手紙と別季節の写真三枚が届き、学生の疑問は追加の説明を招いた。見学写真と比較して一午後は年間労働の一部しか示さないと理解した。最終報告には観察と後で学んだ事の両方を書き、今後も帰校が学習の終わりにならないよう同じ質問段階を設けることにした。

title: 小さな舞台の大きな音

paragraphs.english: A student band practiced in a classroom before performing in a small hall. In the classroom, the guitar and drum sounded balanced. At the hall rehearsal, however, the drum covered the singer's voice. [A] The drummer, Paul, thought the singer should simply use a louder microphone. The teacher asked the band to listen from different seats before changing any equipment. Two members took turns walking around while the others played the same short song. [B] Near the back, words were especially hard to hear. Paul tried softer sticks and moved his drum away from the wall. The singer kept the same microphone level. [C] On the next test, listeners could follow the words more easily. The band wrote down the new arrangement and marked the positions on the floor with removable tape. [D] Paul learned that a performance depended on the room and the audience's position as well as on how the music sounded to the players. They checked the balance again when chairs and guests filled the hall.
paragraphs.translation: 教室では均衡したバンドの音が、小ホールのリハーサルではドラムに歌声が埋もれた。ポールはマイク音量を上げればよいと思ったが、先生は機材変更前に各席で聴かせた。二人ずつ交代して同じ曲を聴くと、聞こえ方は場所で異なり後方ほど歌詞が難しかった。柔らかいスティックにしドラムを壁から離し、マイクは同じにした。次は言葉を聞きやすくなり配置を記録して床を剥がせるテープで印した。演奏者だけでなく室内と聴衆の位置も大事と学び、椅子と客が入った時も再確認した。
